stories.event: Taiwan votes on National Referendum No. 22 on Saturday 28 Nov 2026 alongside the nine-in-one local elections (polls 08:00-16:00 Taipei). The KMT-proposed question, passed by the Legislature 59-51 with TPP support and approved by the CEC on 28 Aug, asks whether voters support the government using nuclear power to revitalize the economy and abolishing the 'nuclear-free homeland' energy policy. It passes if agree votes exceed disagree votes and reach one quarter of the 20,003,835 eligible voters (5,000,959). The 2025 Maanshan restart question, held alone, won 74% yes but only 4.34 million votes at 29.5% turnout; the 2018 nuclear question held with local elections passed with 5.90 million agree votes. The DPP opposes the proposal, though President Lai has said restarts of Kuosheng and Maanshan will be evaluated.

stories.event: Victoria votes on Saturday 28 November 2026 for all 88 Legislative Assembly seats; Labor under Premier Ben Carroll (premier since Allan resigned on 28 July 2026) seeks a fourth term against Jess Wilson's Liberal–National Coalition, with One Nation (Warren Pickering) polling 16–25%. Labor notionally holds 56 seats and the Coalition 29 (2022 TPP 55–45 to Labor); the Coalition needs 16 gains, and on the ABC pendulum the 16th is Monbulk at 7.6%, so a uniform swing needs about 52.6–47.4 TPP (lead +5.2). The final polls give the Coalition a 55–59% TPP (average lead +14.7 over 7 polls: DemosAU 55–45, Newspoll 57.5–42.5, Resolve 59–41, YouGov 58–42, RedBridge 58–42, Roy Morgan 55–45, Agenda C 59–41) and a primary vote of 31–34%, with Labor at 19–25%. Seat projections are YouGov MRP Coalition 55 (ONP 12) and Poll Bludger's model 52 (ONP 11). The main risk is One Nation and independents taking seats on the Coalition's path. Postal votes are admitted until 4 Dec, so the count is incomplete at resolution.

stories.event: ITLOS delivers its Order in Case No. 37, Case concerning hydrocarbon exploitation in the South-West Atlantic Ocean (Argentina v. United Kingdom), Provisional Measures, at noon Hamburg time on Sat 28 Nov 2026 (PR 405). Argentina filed under art. 290(5) on 13 Oct 2026 after starting Annex VII arbitration on 28 Sep; the hearing was 10-11 Nov. Argentina's final submissions ask the UK to stop new exploitation drilling and production infrastructure for Sea Lion (Navitas 65%, Rockhopper 35%; FID 10 Dec 2025), plus information, environment and non-aggravation measures. The UK asks for rejection: the real issue is Falklands sovereignty (no prima facie jurisdiction), and there is no urgency because by formal assurance drilling will not start before 21 Mar 2027 nor extraction before Mar 2028, while the Annex VII tribunal should be constituted by Jan 2027. Both States have art. 298(1)(a) delimitation declarations, which neither side says cover this dispute.

In 2021 ANIE announced an election-night APC turnout of 35.97% (APW 34.39%), revised to 36.58% (APW 34.76%) in the provisional results three days later. The July 2026 legislative elections set a record low turnout of 20.79% on election night (21.24% provisional), after 23% in 2021; parties struggled to fill local lists this autumn.

claims.label: Turnout no higher than in 2021
claims.text: Turnout in Algeria's municipal (APC) elections on Saturday 28 November 2026, as announced on election night, is at or below the 35.97% announced on election night in 2021.
claims.criterion: YES if the final national turnout for the municipal people's assemblies (APC) of 28 Nov 2026 first announced at the close of polls (by ANIE's president, or, if ANIE does not announce it, by the Interior Ministry as the official national figure; normally late on 28 Nov or early 29 Nov, Africa/Algiers) is 35.97% or lower, 35.97% being the comparable figure ANIE announced on election night in 2021 (later revised to 36.58% in the provisional results). NO if it is above 35.97%, or if the elections are not held on 28 Nov 2026. Hourly interim figures and later revisions do not count. If only a combined APC/APW or 'average' figure is given, that figure counts.
claims.publishes: ANIE (or Interior Ministry) press conference at the close of polls, late 28 Nov or early 29 Nov; APS

cs.label: Účast nejvýš jako v roce 2021
cs.text: Účast v alžírských obecních volbách (APC) v sobotu 28. listopadu 2026, jak ji úřady oznámí ve volební noci, bude nejvýše 35,97 %, které byly oznámeny ve volební noci v roce 2021.
cs.criterion: ANO, pokud konečná celostátní účast ve volbách do obecních lidových shromáždění (APC) z 28. listopadu 2026, jak ji poprvé oznámí po uzavření volebních místností předseda ANIE (nebo, neoznámí-li ji ANIE, ministerstvo vnitra jako oficiální celostátní údaj; obvykle pozdě večer 28. listopadu nebo brzy 29. listopadu alžírského času), bude 35,97 % nebo nižší; 35,97 % je srovnatelný údaj, který ANIE oznámila ve volební noci v roce 2021 (v předběžných výsledcích později upravený na 36,58 %). NE, pokud bude vyšší než 35,97 %, nebo pokud se volby 28. listopadu 2026 nekonají. Průběžné hodinové údaje ani pozdější revize se nepočítají. Uvede-li se jen společný údaj za APC a APW nebo „průměrná“ účast, počítá se tento údaj.

agents.reason_blind: Small class 1/4 with no wider class; kept within 15-85%. Start 0.25, up slightly (+0.4 log-odds): locals draw on notable networks and ran ~13 pp above same-year legislative in 2021; new ANIE head pushes participation; more registrants. Against: 2 Jul 2026 legislative record low 20.79% (night), down from ~23% in 2021, so +13 pp gives ~34% < 35.97%; parties struggled to fill lists. Slip 0.003.
agents.reason: Class 1/4 (no wider class). Union adds the view that 2021 was a post-Hirak low, with locals at 44-47% in 2012/2017, and that the authorities are pushing turnout; I give it a little weight (+0.08 log-odds). But 2026 legislative turnout (20.79% night) is below 2021's ~23%. Scaling 2021's locals-to-legislative gap (+13 pp, or x1.56) gives ~32.5-34%, under 35.97%. Slip 0.003. [Figures given for 'turnout above 35.97%' and mirrored here as 0.997 − p, for this claim on the likelier side.]

agents.reason_blind: 2021 pattern: legislatives 23.03% (June) then APC 35.97% on election night (ratio ~1.56). July 2026 legislatives hit a record low 20.79% at close (later 21.24%); same ratio implies ~32-33% for APC. ANIE (Arous) talks up new registrants and more candidates; locals mobilise via local lists, and figures can be generous (2024 presidential), but ANIE reported the July low plainly. Lean NO.

Locals before 2019 ran at 44-47%, and new wilayas, more registrants and an official turnout push (the generous 2024 48% figure) leave real upside. Parties struggled to fill lists.
